text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bank rate hits 3.75 percent: Prime drops to 5.25 percent, lowest level for Canadian borrowers since 1959.
- Reform Party rethinks social spending: More, not less, for health, schools.
- Prime Minister Jean Chretien touts Liberals' fiscal record: Chretien vows 'to stay course'.
- Ontario to sell water, sewage agency: Conservatives seek buyer for firm providing services to millions of residents.
- Dole goes on offensive in debate with Clinton: Republican stresses ethics while President trumpets record.
- 79 die in Guatemala soccer game stampede.
- Ontario Securities Commission in paralysis: Stalemate over creation of national securities watchdog leaves top regulator in limbo.
- Bank of Montreal launches virtual banking division: Mbanx unit to lure customers with personal managers, cash rewards.
- Bond markets losing fear of Canadian debt: Spread between yields in Canada, U.S. dwindling to zero.
- Indonesian dispute hammers Bre-X again: Market shaves C$435 million off value.
- GM, CAW set deadline for deal: Both sides appear ready to break the logjam after two-hour Toronto summit between union's Hargrove and GM chief Jack Smith.
- Rates slide again as economic signals weaken. --
